purpose: Close an open-redirect defect found while assessing ASVS V3.7.2. All three non-production demo-login routes accepted a caller-supplied 'to' destination and validated it with `raw.startsWith('/')`, which a protocol-relative ('//evil.example') or backslash-prefixed ('/\\evil.example') value defeats: both start with one slash and both resolve, under the WHATWG URL algorithm every browser implements, to a foreign origin. /api/auth/demo and /api/auth/demo/role/[role] answer with a Location header; /api/auth/demo/instant/[role] instead writes the destination into an inline script that calls window.location.replace(), so it additionally needs a path-absolute serialization (dot-segment removal turns '/.//evil.example' into the pathname '//evil.example') and JavaScript-string rather than HTML-entity encoding. All three routes are fail-closed in production (demoLoginAllowed() checks NODE_ENV unconditionally first), so this was not reachable in production as currently deployed, but it is a real defect and is fixed rather than left for the gate that happened to mask it.
requiredInvariants: The fix changes only how a redirect destination is validated and serialized. It must not change where any genuinely same-origin destination navigates. The one intended serialization change is on the instant route: its destination was HTML-entity escaped inside a <script> element, where entities are not decoded, so every '&' in a query string reached the browser as a literal '&'; it is now encoded as a JavaScript string literal and arrives intact.

The check must be on the resolved result (does the candidate's resolved origin match the request's own origin), never on a prefix of the raw string; a prefix check is exactly the class of defect being closed.
demoLoginAllowed() and its production fail-closed behaviour are untouched.

New or modified test files must be wired into the CI-gated web-unit step in .github/workflows/ci.yml, per scripts/security/verify-web-unit-coverage.mjs, not silently left unexecuted or added to the exclusion registry.
No product code outside the listed paths changes. No migration, schema, dependency or production configuration changes.
Merge and CI success are not REG.RU production deployment evidence.
ownerRatificationRequired: Scope authorization. This manifest was written by the implementation agent because no approved concurrent scope existed for this branch and scripts/p7-autopilot-guard.sh blocked. It is the repository's declared source-controlled mechanism, but it is self-declared and requires owner ratification in review before it counts as authorization.
acceptance: A protocol-relative or backslash-prefixed destination no longer produces a cross-origin navigation from any of the three routes; each falls back to its safe default.

On the instant route, a destination whose normalized pathname begins with '//' (for example '/.//evil.example') falls back instead of being emitted as a protocol-relative reference, and the destination cannot close the inline script element.
A genuinely same-origin destination, including its query string and fragment, still navigates to the same place.

The mutation checks (restoring the old startsWith('/') prefix logic; removing the '//' guard from toPathAbsoluteReference; restoring the HTML-escaped single-quoted literal) each make the new tests fail; restoring the fix makes them pass again.
node scripts/security/verify-web-unit-coverage.mjs passes with both new/modified test files executed, not excluded.
The exact CI web-unit vitest command (25 files after merging main) passes in full.
